annotations.label: Actor
annotations.comment: Human or organizational agent that owns, operates, or regulates components
annotations.scope_note: Use for humans and organisations that own, operate or regulate components. Automatic acting equipment is a Device (Actuator, Controller), not an Actor.
annotations.dici_definition: Actors represent stakeholders in the energy system including operators, regulators, consumers, and policy makers
examples: A utility company, a grid operator, a municipality, a household, a regulator

annotations.label: Converter
annotations.comment: Component that transforms an input into a different output form (energy or material)
annotations.definition: A machine or installation that converts energy from one form or carrier to another, or transforms materials. The equipment is the Converter; the transformation activity it performs is a ConversionProcess.
examples: Heat pump, boiler, electrolyser, turbine, inverter

annotations.label: Device
annotations.comment: Physical or virtual devices that monitor, control, or measure components in the energy system
annotations.scope_note: Use for monitoring, control and measurement equipment. Machinery that converts or stores energy belongs under Converter or Storage, not Device.
annotations.dici_definition: Devices are components that provide sensing, actuation, measurement, or control capabilities within the energy system
examples: Sensors, meters, controllers, switches, actuators

annotations.label: Energy Carrier
annotations.comment: The medium or commodity form in which energy is stored, transported and consumed
annotations.scope_note: EnergyCarrier is the commodity (what), Flow is its movement (the transfer), Network is the infrastructure it moves through.
annotations.definition: An energy vector: the commodity that carries energy through the system, independent of the infrastructure that moves it.
examples: Electricity, district heat, natural gas, hydrogen, biomass

annotations.label: Energy Consumer
annotations.comment: Component whose primary role is to consume energy
annotations.scope_note: Use for demand-side entities. A component that transforms energy onward rather than consuming it is a Converter.
annotations.definition: A component that takes energy out of the system for an end use. Consumers are the demand side: they receive flows but do not transform them into another carrier.
examples: A building heating load, an EV charging station, an industrial process line

annotations.label: Energy Generator
annotations.comment: Component whose primary role is to produce energy
annotations.scope_note: The generating equipment is an EnergyGenerator (or a Converter subclass such as Turbine); the site it stands on (e.g. a wind park as a place) is a Location.
annotations.definition: A component that injects energy into the system. Generators are the supply side: the equipment that produces an energy carrier from a resource or fuel.
examples: PV plant, diesel genset, CHP unit

annotations.label: Flow
annotations.comment: Represents the movement or transfer of energy, materials, or information between components
annotations.scope_note: A Flow connects a source Component to a destination Component (hasSource / hasDestination) and carries a Resource or EnergyCarrier (carriesResource). Use the typed subclasses (ElectricityFlow, HeatFlow, ...) where one fits.
annotations.dici_definition: A flow captures the dynamic transfer of entities (energy carriers, materials, etc.) between system components, including quantity, direction, and temporal characteristics
examples: Electricity flow from the grid to a building; heat flow from a plant into a district network

annotations.label: Junction
annotations.comment: Component where multiple flows meet or diverge
annotations.dici_definition: Junctions represent nodes where flows can be split, merged, or redirected without transformation
examples: Electrical busbar, pipe tee, district-heating manifold

annotations.label: Location
annotations.comment: Spatial entity representing geographic areas or specific sites
annotations.scope_note: Use as the parent for spatial grouping concepts: a WindPark or a Campus is a Location. Do not use Network (connectivity infrastructure) or Junction (flow nodes) for spatial grouping. Components attach to a Location via dici_onto:locatedAt.
annotations.dici_definition: Locations provide spatial context for components and flows, enabling geographic analysis and constraints
examples: A wind park, a city district, a campus, a building plot, a municipality

annotations.label: Material
annotations.comment: Physical substance handled by the system that is not primarily an energy carrier
annotations.definition: A physical substance moved, stored or processed by the system - water, waste, feedstock - as opposed to an EnergyCarrier, whose role is to carry energy.
examples: Water, waste, construction material, industrial feedstock

annotations.label: Network
annotations.comment: Infrastructure for transporting energy carriers or materials
annotations.scope_note: Network is the connective infrastructure through which flows move; the moving quantity itself is a Flow, and spatial grouping is a Location.
annotations.dici_definition: Networks represent the physical infrastructure that enables flows between components, such as electrical grids, gas pipelines, or district heating networks
examples: Electricity distribution grid, gas pipeline network, district heating network

annotations.label: Observation
annotations.comment: Observed phenomenon or measurement record that stands on its own, without a modelled sensor or piece of equipment behind it
annotations.scope_note: Use when only the observed data matters. If the observing device IS part of the model, attach the data to that device (Sensor, Meter) instead; a single measured property of an existing component stays an Attribute on that component, not an Observation.
annotations.definition: An Observation is a component that carries observed or recorded data about a phenomenon when the observing equipment is not part of the model. The observed values attach to it as ordinary attributes, so data can enter the replica without inventing a device to own it.
examples: A weather record for a site; an observed traffic count on a road; an air-quality reading for a district

annotations.label: Process
annotations.comment: A process that transforms, transports, or modifies flows of energy or materials
annotations.scope_note: A Process is the activity; the equipment performing it is a Component subclass (Converter, Storage, ...).
annotations.dici_definition: A process represents any activity or operation that has input and output flows, including energy conversion, material transformation, or transport operations
examples: Space heating, combustion in a boiler, charging a battery

annotations.label: Resource
annotations.comment: Primary source of energy or material drawn from the environment
annotations.scope_note: The wind blowing over a site is a Resource; the electricity generated from it is an ElectricityCarrier; the machine converting it is a Turbine.
annotations.definition: A natural or primary resource that the system harvests, extracts or depends on, as distinct from the processed energy carriers derived from it.
examples: Wind, solar irradiation, groundwater, coal deposit

annotations.label: Storage
annotations.comment: Component that stores energy or materials over time
annotations.dici_definition: Storage components accumulate and release energy or materials, providing temporal flexibility to the system
examples: Battery, hot water tank, pumped hydro reservoir, hydrogen store

annotations.label: Energy Converter
annotations.comment: Converter transforming energy between carriers or forms
examples: Heat pump, boiler, fuel cell, inverter, wind turbine generator

annotations.label: Material Converter
annotations.comment: Converter transforming material inputs into different material outputs
examples: Waste incinerator, biogas digester, recycling plant

annotations.label: Actuator
annotations.comment: Device that converts control signals into physical action
annotations.dici_definition: Actuators are devices that produce motion or control mechanisms based on input signals
examples: Valve actuator, damper motor, relay

annotations.label: Controller
annotations.comment: Device that manages and coordinates other devices or processes
annotations.dici_definition: Controllers implement control logic and coordinate the operation of other system components
examples: Thermostat, building management system, SCADA controller

annotations.label: Meter
annotations.comment: Device that measures and records consumption or production of resources
annotations.scope_note: Meters record cumulative consumption or production over time; instantaneous physical quantities are measured by Sensors.
annotations.dici_definition: Meters measure cumulative quantities like energy consumption, flow volumes, or resource usage over time
examples: Electricity meter, gas meter, heat meter

annotations.label: Sensor
annotations.comment: Device that measures physical quantities and converts them to signals
annotations.dici_definition: Sensors detect and respond to inputs from the physical environment, providing data for monitoring and control
examples: Temperature sensor, pressure sensor, anemometer, pyranometer

annotations.label: Switch
annotations.comment: Device that can interrupt or divert the flow of energy or materials
annotations.dici_definition: Switches control the routing or interruption of flows in the system
examples: Relay, circuit breaker, transfer switch

annotations.label: Electricity Carrier
annotations.comment: Energy carrier for electrical energy
examples: Grid electricity, self-generated PV electricity

annotations.label: Fuel Carrier
annotations.comment: Combustible energy carrier
examples: Natural gas, heating oil, wood pellets, hydrogen

annotations.label: Thermal Energy Carrier
annotations.comment: Energy carrier transporting thermal energy (heat or cold)

annotations.label: Energy Carrier Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of energy carriers between components
examples: Electricity flow, heat flow, gas flow

annotations.label: Information Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of information or control signals between components
examples: Sensor readings sent to a controller; a control signal sent to an actuator

annotations.label: Material Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of materials between components
examples: Waste stream, water supply, feedstock delivery

annotations.label: Weather Observation
annotations.comment: Observation of weather conditions at a place, independent of any weather-station equipment
annotations.scope_note: For a modelled weather station or sensor (the device), use Sensor. For the harvestable resource itself, use SolarResource or Wind. A bundle of many weather variables in one artefact (a weather file) is a CompositeWeatherObservation.
annotations.definition: An observation carrying observed or recorded weather data (temperature, wind, irradiance, precipitation and similar) for a place, used when no weather station or sensor is modelled.
examples: Observed hourly temperature and wind speed for a site in 2024

annotations.label: Conversion Process
annotations.comment: Process that converts one form of energy to another
examples: Gas to heat in a boiler; electricity to heat in a heat pump

annotations.label: Storage Process
annotations.comment: Process that stores and releases energy or materials over time
examples: Charging and discharging a battery; filling a thermal store

annotations.label: Transport Process
annotations.comment: Process that transports energy or materials without transformation
examples: Pumping water through a pipe; transmitting electricity over a line

annotations.label: Non Renewable Resource
annotations.comment: Finite resource that does not replenish on a human timescale
examples: Coal, crude oil, natural gas reserves

annotations.label: Renewable Resource
annotations.comment: Resource that replenishes naturally on a human timescale
examples: Wind, solar irradiation, hydro, geothermal heat

annotations.label: Energy Storage
annotations.comment: Storage holding energy for later use
examples: Battery, thermal storage tank, hydrogen storage

annotations.label: Material Storage
annotations.comment: Storage holding materials
examples: Water reservoir, silo, warehouse, fuel depot

annotations.label: Turbine
annotations.comment: Rotary energy converter extracting mechanical work from a moving fluid
annotations.scope_note: A WindTurbine extension class belongs here (under Turbine), while the wind park it stands in is a Location and the wind it harvests is a Wind resource.
examples: A wind turbine in a wind park; a steam turbine in a CHP plant

annotations.label: Damper
annotations.comment: Actuator that controls air flow

annotations.label: Valve
annotations.comment: Actuator that controls fluid flow

annotations.label: Electricity Meter
annotations.comment: Meter recording cumulative electrical energy consumption or production

annotations.label: Gas Meter
annotations.comment: Meter recording cumulative gas volume consumed

annotations.label: Heat Meter
annotations.comment: Meter recording cumulative thermal energy delivered

annotations.label: Flow Sensor
annotations.comment: Sensor measuring volumetric or mass flow rate

annotations.label: Power Sensor
annotations.comment: Sensor measuring instantaneous electrical or thermal power

annotations.label: Pressure Sensor
annotations.comment: Sensor measuring pressure

annotations.label: Temperature Sensor
annotations.comment: Sensor measuring temperature

annotations.label: Circuit Breaker
annotations.comment: Switch that automatically interrupts electrical flow for safety

annotations.label: Gaseous Fuel Carrier
annotations.comment: Fuel carrier in gaseous form
examples: Natural gas, biogas, hydrogen

annotations.label: Liquid Fuel Carrier
annotations.comment: Fuel carrier in liquid form
examples: Heating oil, diesel, biofuel

annotations.label: Solid Fuel Carrier
annotations.comment: Fuel carrier in solid form
examples: Wood chips, pellets, coal

annotations.label: Cold Carrier
annotations.comment: Thermal energy carrier delivering cooling
examples: Chilled water, brine

annotations.label: Heat Carrier
annotations.comment: Thermal energy carrier delivering heat
examples: District heating water, steam

annotations.label: Electricity Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of electrical energy between components

annotations.label: Gas Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of gaseous fuel between components

annotations.label: Heat Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of thermal energy between components

annotations.label: Liquid Fuel Flow
annotations.comment: Flow of liquid fuel between components

annotations.label: Composite Weather Observation
annotations.comment: Weather observation bundling several weather variables into one artefact, typically a weather file
annotations.scope_note: Reference the file from an attribute via hasDataPath. A single observed weather variable (one temperature series) belongs on a WeatherObservation as an ordinary attribute instead.
annotations.definition: A weather observation whose value is a multi-variable artefact (temperature, irradiance, wind, humidity and more in one dataset) rather than a single observed quantity. The artefact is usually an external weather file referenced from an attribute via hasDataPath.
examples: An EPW weather file for Zurich backing a building simulation; a TMY3 dataset for a site

annotations.label: Solar Resource
annotations.comment: Solar irradiation as a harvestable renewable energy resource

annotations.label: Wind Resource
annotations.comment: The wind as a harvestable renewable energy resource
annotations.scope_note: Use for the wind resource itself. A wind park (the site) maps to Location; a wind turbine (the machine) maps to Turbine; forecast wind speeds are DynamicAttributes with a FutureTimeSeries.
examples: The wind resource at a wind park site, characterised by speed and direction profiles
